vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: contextclear
Version: 1.1.0

The contextclear skill is a standard observability tool designed to monitor AI agent performance, token usage, and costs. The included Python script (scripts/report.py) reports numerical metrics and status codes to a dedicated API (api.contextclear.com) and does not exfiltrate sensitive files, environment variables, or raw conversation content. The instructions in SKILL.md are consistent with the tool's stated purpose and do not contain malicious prompt injections or unauthorized execution commands.

llm.summary: The skill's code and docs match the stated purpose (reporting agent metrics to an external ContextClear API), but there are coherence and privacy concerns: the skill requires an API key that isn't declared in the registry metadata, instructs storing secrets in plaintext, and is published with an unknown/undeclared source/homepage.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (agent wellness reporting) aligns with the included scripts and API reference: report.py posts metrics to api.contextclear.com and SKILL.md shows the same endpoints. However the registry metadata lists no primary credential or required env vars even though the script expects CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (or CLI flags). The primary credential should be declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to 'auto-report metrics after LLM calls' but the provided script is a CLI tool — there is no automatic runtime integration code shown. SKILL.md also tells users to add API keys and agent IDs to a HEARTBEAT.md file (plaintext), which is a privacy/security concern. Instructions otherwise only reference the external ContextClear API (no unexpected system-wide access), but the storage of secrets in a markdown file and the claim of auto-reporting without an integration are inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided and the skill is instruction + a small Python script. That is low-risk from an install perspective (nothing is downloaded at install time). The script uses only Python stdlib urllib, so no extra packages are installed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry declares no required env vars or primary credential, but report.py clearly reads CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (or accepts them via CLI). Requiring an API key for an external telemetry service is expected, but the omission from the metadata is an inconsistency. Also, SKILL.md's recommended practice (putting API key in HEARTBEAT.md) encourages storing secrets in an unprotected file — disproportionate risk for a monitoring tool. The skill will send potentially sensitive telemetry (tokens, errors, costs) to a third party.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and has no installation that persists code into unusual locations. It runs as a CLI script when invoked; autonomous invocation by the agent platform is allowed by default but not specifically escalated by this skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate agent-monitoring client, but proceed cautiously. Before installing or using it: (1) Verify the ContextClear service and owner (there's no homepage/source listed in the registry); confirm privacy and data retention policies. (2) Do not store API keys in plaintext files like HEARTBEAT.md — use environment variables or a secrets manager instead. (3) Update the registry metadata or ask the publisher to declare required env vars (CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY, CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID) and the primary credential. (4) Be aware that the script will send metrics (token counts, errors, costs, etc.) to api.contextclear.com; review the exact fields sent and remove any fields you consider sensitive. (5) If you cannot verify the publisher, run the script in an isolated environment or sandbox and consider auditing network traffic to confirm endpoints. (6) If you need automatic reporting integrated into your agent runtime, implement and review the integration yourself rather than relying on the SKILL.md claim of auto-reporting.
